names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 15 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Στέφανος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Σουρόζας», with the rank word and the see left off. The page glosses the name itself, «(από το στέφανος) = ο αθλοφόρος, ο άξιος στεφάνου νίκης».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s second heading for 15. децембар ст. ст., „Свети Стефан, исповедник сурожски.“ — with «Свети» left off, which §5 says is not a rank, and «исповедник» left off, that being the `confessor` grade §5 maps and which this upgrade puts into `types`. What is left is the forename and the see’s adjective, and that is the fullest form the calendar gives. TWO READINGS ARE IN THIS FORM AND BOTH ARE STATED. First, the toponymic adjective is CAPITALISED here, where the Prologue prints it lower case because it stands mid-sentence after the rank word; that is the habit this corpus’s own Serbian forms already keep — «Стефан Дечански», «Сава Сторожевски», «Тихон Задонски», «Серафим Саровски» — and the adjective is kept rather than dropped because dropping it would leave a bare «Стефан», which `fk.mjs` measures at a very large fold. Second, the adjective is a see and §6 says a see is stripped; it is kept because it is the whole of what tells this Stephen from the corpus’s other hundred and sixty, and because the alternative is that bare fold. THE FOLD WAS MEASURED BEFORE THE FORM WAS WRITTEN: `fk.mjs` puts the key `стефан сурожски` at NO other holder.

The calendar’s own name page for him is «Святитель Стефан Сурожский, архиепископ, исповедник»; the rank words are stripped and the epithet kept, the day line itself declining the forename, the grade and the see. `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

feast.note: The same menologion day this folder’s other rows already carry, so there is no second day and none is noted. The line closes «(VIII)», the eighth century, which is the century the folder’s `death` already holds as its last quarter from the Ohrid Prologue’s «крајем VIII века»; it is consistent and wider, so it replaces nothing. The reading this calendar links, `/Life/life3123.htm`, was NOT opened; this folder’s life is already written out of its other sources. The day page’s fifth and sixth hymn blocks are under his name, and THE TROPARION ADDRESSES HIM «священномучениче» WHILE ITS OWN TITLE CALLS HIM «святителя … исповедника», and the calendar’s line and name page call him confessor; the hymns are titled for him by name and see and are his, and the difference of title is the source’s own and is not resolved here.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 декабря ст. ст. — «Свт. Стефана исп., архиеп. Сурожского (VIII).»

attestations.note: Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Στέφανος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Σουρόζας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 15 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. **The whole of the page's text is one sentence and it is a refusal to tell the life, not a refusal to vouch for the man: «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Ρώσου Αγίου.»** There is no asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου…», which is the mark this corpus refuses on. No year, no place beyond the see, no relic, no hymn. The corpus already keeps `sabbas-of-sourozh` for the same see, on 2 Απριλίου; nothing in this line joins the two men and nothing is drafted from the coincidence of the see. The `russian` row is left `undocumented` although the page calls him a Russian saint, because days.pravoslavie.ru was not read.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.12.2025 (15. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети Стефан, исповедник сурожски.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. **This row is the reason the folder now has a life at all.** saint.gr’s whole entry for him was «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Ρώσου Αγίου» — we have no details of the life of the Russian saint — and the folder said so and stopped. This book gives: Cappadocia for his birth; his upbringing at Constantinople with the patriarch Saint Germanus; a withdrawal into solitude and a life hidden from the world; an ANGEL who made him known to Germanus and commanded that he be set bishop of the city of Sourozh, which the book glosses «(садашњи Судак на Криму)», the present Sudak in the Crimea; many turned to Christianity; bitter suffering under Leo the Isaurian FOR THE ICONS; a prophecy to that emperor of his swift ruin; a return to his own diocese after the emperor’s evil death; and a peaceful end at the close of the eighth century. `types_add`: `confessor`, from the heading’s own «исповедник», which §5 maps to that word and which is the ground of the whole entry — the iconoclast persecution he survived. `dates` ADDED: a death in the late eighth century, the folder having carried none. `related_add`: `germanus-of-constantinople`, who is this saint’s teacher and his consecrator in this book’s own telling, and whose folder takes the answering row in this same commit. NO `locations`: Cappadocia, Constantinople and Sudak are three places and the folder has never held a coordinate. The emperor Leo the Isaurian is no folder this corpus holds. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: The first date this folder has carried, and the Ohrid Prologue is the only source in it that gives one. Охридски пролог за 15. децембар ст. ст.: „По злој смрти овога злог цара Стефан би враћен на своју епархију, где пасе стадо своје богоугодно и сконча мирно, крајем VIII века.“ — after the evil death of that evil emperor Stephen was given back to his own diocese, where he shepherded his flock in a way pleasing to God and died in peace at the END of the eighth century. The bounds are the last quarter of that century, which is what «крајем» says and no more; saint.gr gave no year at all, having nothing of his life. The book’s own Leo the Isaurian, who reigned to 741, is consistent with it and was not used to narrow it, an emperor’s reign not being a year of death.

hymns.text: Яко святитель со Безплотными единожитель быв,/ священномучениче Стефане,/ восприем бо Крест яко оружие,/ и став крепко сопротив иконоукорителя и духоборцев,/ не покланяющихся пречистому образу Христа Бога нашего,/ и отсекл еси всяку ересь лукавых./ Того ради прием мучения венец,/ избавил еси град твой Сурож от всякия неприязни./ И ныне молим тя, святе,/ да избавиши нас от всяких злых искушений, и бед,/ и вечныя муки.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 декабря ст. ст. — «Тропарь святителя Стефана исповедника, архиепископа Сурожского», глас 4. His own proper: it names him, his see and the iconoclasm he stood against. Its body addresses him «священномучениче» where its title and the day line call him confessor, and both are left as the page has them.

english.text: As a hierarch thou wast made a fellow-dweller with the bodiless powers, O hieromartyr Stephen; for taking up the Cross as a weapon thou didst stand firm against the reviler of icons and against those who fight the Spirit, who would not bow before the most pure image of Christ our God, and thou didst cut off every heresy of the evil-minded. Wherefore, having received the crown of suffering, thou didst deliver thy city of Sourozh from all enmity. And now we entreat thee, O holy one, deliver us from all evil temptations, and from troubles, and from eternal torment.

hymns.text: Вышняго силою, священне, укрепився,/ царева низложил еси иконоборная шатания;/ днесь Сурожу и нам верным предлежат/ слава и богатство — святыя твоя мощи,/ ихже свыше дароносят Ангельстии чинове,/ песньми и пением славословят тя,/ великий священный Стефане.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 декабря ст. ст. — «Кондак святителя Стефана исповедника, архиепископа Сурожского», глас 3. His own proper: it names him and his city and the relics kept there.

english.text: Strengthened by the power of the Most High, O sacred one, thou didst cast down the emperor’s iconoclast ragings; and today there lie before Sourozh and before us the faithful a glory and a treasure, thy holy relics, which the angelic orders bear as a gift from on high, and with hymns and singing they glorify thee, O great and sacred Stephen.
